what_happened: On a design job, the user corrected Athena's accepted reading. Criterion 9 limited which files the job could change, but it left out CHANGELOG.md. The changelog default adds an entry to that file, so a job that followed the default would have broken the criterion. The user asked for CHANGELOG.md to be added to Criterion 9 and said the rest of the reading was right.
cause: When the reading writes a scope-limit criterion, it lists only the files the request names. It does not add the files that Athena's own defaults will touch, such as the changelog entry. Nothing compares the allowed-file list with the files the defaults write before the reading is accepted. So the gap showed up only when the user read the reading. If it had not, the verifier would have rejected the job later for an out-of-scope edit.
prevention: Add a check at reading acceptance. For any criterion that limits which files may change, the check builds the set of files that Athena's defaults always write, such as CHANGELOG.md, and compares it with the allowed list. If a default file is missing, the reading is rejected or the file is added automatically. Better still, scope-limit criteria should be generated from the request's deliverables plus a fixed list of default-written files, not written freehand.
proposed_request: When Athena accepts a reading that has a criterion limiting which files a job may change, check the allowed-file list against the files Athena's defaults always write, starting with the CHANGELOG.md entry. If a default-written file is missing from the list, add it automatically or refuse the reading with a message naming the file. Add a test that shows a reading with a scope-limit criterion that omits CHANGELOG.md is caught, and a reading that includes it is accepted.
